identity: University of Groningen, English BSc Applied Mathematics (Technische Wiskunde), RIO 56965, registry row 228.

WBMA003-05.title: Calculus 1
WBMA003-05.priorKnowledge: The course builds on high school mathematics: algebra, (analytic) geometry, functions, and trigonometry. It is important to have a solid foundation in these areas and therefore the course starts with a test to assess basic mathematical skills (BMS). If this test result is unsatisfactory, several compulsory practicals follow, after which a second BMS test is offered.

WBMA020-05.title: Linear Algebra 1
WBMA020-05.priorKnowledge: This course is the first Linear Algebra course of the curriculum and builds on high school knowledge of Mathematics.

WBMA012-05.title: Analysis
WBMA012-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the courses Calculus 1 and Sets and Numbers.

WBMA052-05.title: Introduction to Graph Theory
WBMA052-05.priorKnowledge: No prerequisites besides mathematics at the level of Dutch VWO.

WBMA029-05.title: Calculus 2
WBMA029-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus 1 and Linear Algebra 1.

WBMA053-05.title: Scientific Programming
WBMA053-05.priorKnowledge: For Unit 1, the course builds on knowledge obtained in Calculus 1. For Unit 2, background knowledge as obtained in Linear Algebra 1 and Calculus 2 is assumed.

WBMA035-05.title: Linear Algebra 2
WBMA035-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Linear Algebra 1 (WBMA020-05).

WBMA060-05.title: Mechanics and Relativity
WBMA060-05.priorKnowledge: It is assumed that students have a solid understanding of the topics typically covered in Calculus 1 and 2. This includes a good grasp of vectors and the geometry of space, such as three-dimensional coordinate systems, dot and cross products, as well as multivariable calculus in three dimensions. High school physics would be also useful.

WBMA043-05.title: Linear Systems
WBMA043-05.priorKnowledge: The course assumes prior knowledge in linear algebra (as offered in the courses Linear Algebra 1 and 2).

WBMA046-05.title: Probability Theory
WBMA046-05.priorKnowledge: The course assumes prior knowledge from: Calculus 1 & 2, Analysis, Sets and Numbers

WBMA040-05.title: First-year Project Applied Mathematics
WBMA040-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired in the first-year (depending on the chosen topic)

WBMA036-05.title: Metric and Topological Spaces
WBMA036-05.priorKnowledge: The course assumes knowledge from Analysis and Linear Algebra.

WBMA009-05.title: Statistics
WBMA009-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge from the course Probability Theory.

WBMA054-05.title: Introduction to Optimization
WBMA054-05.priorKnowledge: The course assumes knowledge from: Linear algebra 1 (WBMA020-05), Calculus 2 (WBMA029-05), Analysis (WBMA012-05), Scientific Programming (WBMA053-05) and programming (ideally in python).

WBMA018-05.title: Complex Analysis
WBMA018-05.priorKnowledge: Knowledge assumed: Calculus, Analysis and Metric Spaces

WBMA022-05.title: Multivariable Analysis
WBMA022-05.priorKnowledge: This course assumes prior knowledge from: Linear Algebra 1,2 and Calculus 1,2

WBMA061-05.title: Differential Equations in Science and En
WBMA061-05.priorKnowledge: Knowledge assumed: Linear algebra (matrix notation, computation of eigenvalues) as taught in Linear Algebra 1. Calculus and multivariate calculus (partial derivatives, integration, index notation) as taught in Calculus 1 and 2. Ordinary differential equations (notation, solution of linear systems of ODEs) as taught in Linear Systems.

WBMA033-05.title: Functional Analysis
WBMA033-05.priorKnowledge: Linear Algebra 1, Linear Algebra 2, Analysis, Metric and Topological Spaces. Knowledge from Complex Analysis is helpful, but not strictly necessary.

WBMA062-05.title: Numerical Analysis
WBMA062-05.priorKnowledge: The course assumes knowledge from: Linear Algebra 1 (WBMA020-05); Calculus 1 (WBMA003-05); Calculus 2 (WBMA029-05); Analysis (WBMA012-05); Scientific Programming (WBMA053-05); Dynamical Systems (WBMA031-05) or Differential Equations in Science and Engineering (WBMA061-05).

WBMA008-05.title: Partial Differential Equations
WBMA008-05.priorKnowledge: Background knowledge from ordinary differential equations is required (as taught in Calculus 1 and Multivariable Analysis). Knowledge of Functional Analysis is helpful.

WBMA007-05.title: Mathematical Modelling
WBMA007-05.priorKnowledge: Knowledge assumed: Calculus and Linear Algebra from the first-year programme, Differential Equations and Vectorcalculus.

WBMA004-05.title: Computational Methods of Science
WBMA004-05.priorKnowledge:
Prior knowledge assumed: Numerical Analysis (Python, Interpolation, Num. integration, ODE).
Calculus 2 (Multivariate calculus, Gauss theorem, etc).
Linear Algebra 1 and 2 (matrices, linear spaces, eigenvalues).
Functional Analysis.
Familiarity with some basic notions for PDEs (e.g. classification of PDE, well-posedness).

WBMA027-05.title: Project Systems Theory
WBMA027-05.priorKnowledge: This course builds on the Linear Systems course, hence proper knowledge of the concepts and ideas from that course are necessary to successfully follow this course.

WBMA055-05.title: Project Mathematical Modelling
WBMA055-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from previous courses on mathematical and numerical modelling, such as Differential Equations in Science and Engineering (WBMA061), Mathematical Modeling (WBMA007), Partial Differential Equations (WBMA008), Numerical Analysis (WBMA062) and Computational Methods of Science
(WBMA004).

WBMA063-05.title: Numerical Linear Algebra
WBMA063-05.priorKnowledge: Knowledge and skill in handling basic numerical techniques and programming in Python as taught in the course Numerical Mathematics I/Numerical Analysis and good knowledge of linear algebra and vector analysis is necessary.

WBMA001-05.title: Advanced Systems Theory
WBMA001-05.priorKnowledge: Knowledge assumed: Linear Algebra 1, Linear Algebra 2 and Linear Systems

WBMA049-05.title: Mathematics & Society: Ethical and Professional Aspects
WBMA049-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes that some knowledge and basic experience in skills like academic writing, presenting, finding scientific literature and collaborating are acquired in the first years of the BSc program and high school.

WBMA028-05.title: Statistical Modelling
WBMA028-05.priorKnowledge: This course builds on Statistics in the second year. Prior knowledge assumed: Students have a background in the courses Probability Theory and Statistics.

WBMA056-05.title: Preparation Bachelor's Project
WBMA056-05.priorKnowledge: This course assumes a (basic) knowledge of second-year mathematics and builds on the research, presentation and writing skills learned in the First-year Project.

WBMA901-15.title: Bachelor's Project Applied Mathematics
WBMA901-15.priorKnowledge: Completion of the First year of the degree programme, 150 ECTS earned in the Bachelor’s programme (study programme approved by BOE), approval of the career portfolio and completion of Preparation Bachelor's Project (WBMA056, per. 2A).

components: The Applied Mathematics project is one of two first-year choices. Students draw on first-year mathematics to investigate an applied problem.
Differential Equations in Science and Engineering
One of the two required modelling or systems project choices illustrated here. Uses earlier differential equations, numerical methods and scientific computing.
The second project choice illustrated here. Builds on first-year Linear Systems.
One of two advanced choices illustrated here. Uses earlier linear algebra and numerical analysis, including Python.
The other advanced choice illustrated here. Builds on Linear Algebra 1 and 2 and Linear Systems.
Mathematics & Society: Ethical and Professional Aspects
The example uses Statistical Modelling as the elective. It builds on Probability Theory and Statistics.
Builds on the first-year project and second-year mathematics and must be completed before the bachelor’s project.
Requires completion of year one and 150 EC in the degree, including project preparation, with an approved study programme and career portfolio. Students must also enrol in the project.
The standard route includes 15 EC of minor space. The courses depend on the minor chosen.
sourceUse: Appendices II–IV control the ordinary 165 EC major and 15 EC minor. Alternative 30 EC abroad or education minors modify the major and are not used. The project specific to the named degree is the first-year illustration. Both upper-year project and advanced choices follow the first two entries in Appendix IV. Statistical Modelling is the first eligible Applied Mathematics elective outside the already selected options. The minor is open.

progression.firstYear: Calculus 1, Linear Algebra 1 and Sets and Numbers precede Analysis, Calculus 2 and Scientific Programming. Linear Algebra 2 in block 2a precedes Linear Systems in 2b. The Applied Mathematics project and Probability Theory run in 2b.
progression.secondYear: Year one Probability Theory precedes Statistics. Metric and Topological Spaces in 1a precedes Complex Analysis. The first-year calculus and linear algebra sequence prepares for Multivariable Analysis and Differential Equations in 1b. The latter and prior scientific programming support Numerical Analysis in 2a. Numerical Analysis and Functional Analysis precede Computational Methods of Science in 2b, which also lists familiarity with basic PDE concepts. The formal sequence places the dedicated Partial Differential Equations course in the same block. Project Systems Theory can be taken in year two block 2a after Linear Systems, giving 60 EC in year two.
progression.thirdYear: Numerical Linear Algebra, Advanced Systems Theory and Statistical Modelling fit autumn block 1b. Their prior numerical, systems, probability and statistics units precede them. 15 EC of minor room can be used in autumn, allowing 150 EC by spring. Project Mathematical Modelling, Mathematics & Society and Preparation Bachelor’s Project fit block 2a after the corresponding modelling, research and writing preparation, followed by the 15 EC individual project in 2b.
progression.research: Appendix IV and the dated WBMA901-15 entry together establish the completed first year, 150 EC including Preparation Bachelor’s Project, approved study programme and career portfolio, and project enrolment. The illustrated term order permits 165 EC before the project if autumn minor and spring 2a units have been completed.
